A1.justification: Both complete 21-page PDFs describe CBGBench. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the main text, equations, figures, tables, references and Appendices A–C are available and directly comparable.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational benchmark experiments on de novo generation and four lead-optimization tasks, together with receptor case studies and supplementary analyses (Section 5 and Appendix C).

after.justification: v2 retains these original computational results, including comparative performance, receptor case studies and molecular-validity results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The graph-completion formulation, model implementations, lead-optimization adaptations and reconstruction procedures are unchanged (Sections 2 and 5; Appendices B and C.3). The DiffSBDD typography edit does not change a method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CrossDocked2020 for de novo generation and the same four lead-optimization tasks. The ADRB1 and DRD3 case studies and GEOM-DRUG control samples are also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments: ten methods for de novo generation, five for lead optimization and seven for the receptor case studies (Tables 3–8; Figures 3–4 and 7).

E3.justification: Table 2 retains identical splits and sample counts. Training budgets, architecture controls, generation of 100 molecules per test pocket, docking modes, metrics, case-study sampling and validity procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The molecule-size versus binding-energy analysis in Appendix A.2, receptor case studies and diagnostic analyses in Appendix C are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity or robustness experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: The same distribution plots, correlation summaries and ranking procedures are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or formal significance-test results.

E6.justification: All numerical tables, plotted results and reported findings match. For example, Table 7 ranks TargetDiff first and DecompDiff second in both versions, while Table 19 retains their validity values of 0.96 and 0.89, respectively.

T1.justification: The binding-graph definitions in Section 2.1, metric definitions in Section 4 and Appendix A.3, and validity criterion in Appendix C.3 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claim scope: the graph-completion formulation, modular benchmark, method taxonomy, expanded task coverage and comprehensive empirical evaluation.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning chemical-bond modeling, domain knowledge, clashes and task difficulty are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning CNN integration and reliance on computational metrics without wet-lab validation.

D1.justification: Data-construction rules, implementation and configuration disclosures, reconstruction details, code-access information and the Apache 2.0 license remain unchanged, including the codebase description in Appendix B.

R1.justification: All 61 reference entries and the related-work taxonomy and positioning in Section 2.2 are unchanged. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research is added or removed.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes affiliation 2 from 'Deep Potential' to 'DP Technology' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Appendix C.3 restyles one DiffSBDD mention from monospace to small capitals. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 19 tables and seven figures retain identical displays, captions and placement. Page organization is unchanged; the localized affiliation and body-text edits do not alter figure, table or document layout.

improvement.justification: v2 changes only an affiliation name, the version stamp and one method-name typography instance. The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so these isolated editorial edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
